transcript_evidence.title: GEV_transcript.txt
transcript_evidence.claim: On the earnings call, management said backlog has grown from $116 billion at spin to $163 billion, including an 80% increase in equipment backlog at better margins.
transcript_evidence.summary: Management emphasized both backlog growth and improved margin quality in equipment backlog.
transcript_evidence.excerpt: Since our spin, we launched with a $116 billion backlog. We have grown this backlog to $163 billion with an 80% increase in our equipment backlog at considerably better margins.

transcript_evidence.title: GEV_transcript.txt
transcript_evidence.claim: Management accelerated its expectation for GE Vernova to reach $200 billion of backlog to 2027 from the prior expectation of 2028.
transcript_evidence.summary: Management pulled forward its backlog milestone, citing rapid recent backlog additions.
transcript_evidence.excerpt: In the last 90 days, we have added $13 billion to our total backlog and now expect to reach $200 billion in backlog in 2027, versus our previous expectation of 2028.

transcript_evidence.title: GEV_transcript.txt
transcript_evidence.claim: Management said Gas Power demand and pricing trends remain favorable for both equipment and services, with demand global and diversified by customer.
transcript_evidence.summary: Management described constructive demand and pricing conditions in Gas Power.
transcript_evidence.excerpt: In Gas Power, we continue to see significant demand and favorable pricing trends for both equipment and services. This demand is global and spans a diverse set of customers.

transcript_evidence.title: GEV_transcript.txt
transcript_evidence.claim: GE Vernova signed 21 GW of new gas turbine agreements in Q1 across countries including the U.S., Vietnam, Mexico, Brazil, and Canada, increasing total GW under contract from 83 to 100 sequentially.
transcript_evidence.summary: The call provided country-level examples of gas turbine demand and quantified sequential contract growth.
transcript_evidence.excerpt: We saw continued strength in new gas turbine agreements in Q1, signing 21 gigawatts in countries like the U.S., Vietnam, Mexico, Brazil, and Canada to grow our total gigawatts under contract from 83 to 100 gigawatts sequentially.

transcript_evidence.title: GEV_transcript.txt
transcript_evidence.claim: Management said roughly 20% of total Gas Power GW under contract explicitly supports data centers, while about 80% is with traditional customers.
transcript_evidence.summary: Management quantified data-center-related exposure within the Gas Power contract base.
transcript_evidence.excerpt: Approximately 80% of our total gigawatts under contract are with traditional customers with the remaining 20% explicitly supporting data centers.

transcript_evidence.title: GEV_transcript.txt
transcript_evidence.claim: Management expects 2026 gas turbine orders to be priced 10 to 20 points higher than Q4 2025 orders on a dollar-per-kW basis.
transcript_evidence.summary: Management gave explicit positive pricing commentary for 2026 gas turbine orders.
transcript_evidence.excerpt: On pricing, we expect our orders in 2026 to be priced 10 to 20 points higher than our Q4 2025 orders on a dollar per kW basis.

transcript_evidence.title: GEV_transcript.txt
transcript_evidence.claim: Management said quarter-to-date April Power equipment order value already exceeded all of Q1 2026, and expects 10 to 15 GW of contracts in Q2.
transcript_evidence.summary: Management indicated strong intra-quarter order momentum and raised/confirmed near-term contract expectations.
transcript_evidence.excerpt: Our momentum has continued into April. Quarter-to-date, we have booked more Power equipment orders in terms of value than we did in all of Q1 2026. On pricing, we expect our orders in 2026 to be priced 10 to 20 points higher than our Q4 2025 orders on a dollar per kW basis. We now expect to book 10 to 15 gigawatts of contracts in Q2 and to end 2026 with at least 110 gigawatts under contract.

transcript_evidence.title: GEV_transcript.txt
transcript_evidence.claim: GE Vernova said it has installed over 280 new machines in Gas Power factories and remains on track to reach 20 GW of annualized output by March.
transcript_evidence.summary: Management described tangible manufacturing capacity additions to support future gas power output.
transcript_evidence.excerpt: On production capacity, we now have installed over 280 new machines in our Gas Power factories and remain on track to reach 20 gigawatts of annualized output by March.

transcript_evidence.title: GEV_transcript.txt
transcript_evidence.claim: Management expects delivering the current backlog later this decade to create a larger and more profitable service book benefiting the 2030s and beyond.
transcript_evidence.summary: Management linked equipment backlog delivery to longer-term service revenue and profitability expansion.
transcript_evidence.excerpt: Delivering on our growing backlog in the second half of this decade will lead to a larger, and even more profitable, service book that will benefit us in the 2030s and beyond.

transcript_evidence.title: GEV_transcript.txt
transcript_evidence.claim: Management said the OPG Darlington SMR project in Canada received recent regulatory approvals and is nearing basemat installation, which it called a critical milestone for the first SMR in construction in North America.
transcript_evidence.summary: The call highlighted a concrete nuclear SMR project milestone and regulatory progress.
transcript_evidence.excerpt:
On the nuclear front, let us start with our operational progress in Canada on Unit 1 of the SMR project at OPGs Darlington site. With the recent regulatory approvals received by our customer, installation will soon begin on the 2 million-pound basemat, a pedestal that will serve as the reactors foundation.

This is a critical milestone and serves as a great illustration of the progress we are making on the first SMR in construction in North America.
